layout.layout: The deer population is in the center. Births are on the left with the reinforcing loop, marked R. Deaths are on the right with the balancing loop, marked B.

B.author_explanation: More deer means more deaths each year, and more deaths reduce the population, which slows growth.
B.name: deaths loop
steps_in_order: When Deer population goes up, Deer deaths per year goes up.
When Deer deaths per year goes up, Deer population goes down.
B.what_it_means: This is a balancing loop: it pushes back against change and moves the system toward a limit.

R.author_explanation: More deer means more births each year, and more births mean even more deer, so the population grows.
R.name: births loop
steps_in_order: When Deer population goes up, Deer births per year goes up.

R.what_it_means: This is a reinforcing loop: a change keeps amplifying itself, causing growth or collapse.

B four point one.name: infrastructure rehabilitation
steps_in_order: When Water shortage goes up, Need for rehabilitation goes up.
When Need for rehabilitation goes up, Rehabilitation goes up. This takes time (delay).
When Rehabilitation goes up, Formal infrastructure aging goes down.

When Infrastructure capacity goes up, Formal supply goes up.
When Formal supply goes up, Water shortage goes down.
